physicalNotes: Radius 13.762 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: radius 13.762 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 843.922 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.91) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 9,574,223 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8392 +/- 4070 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: effective temperature 8392 +/- 4070 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.113) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.

sources.position: Gaia DR3 source 66714384142368256 (Gaia Collaboration 2023, A&A 674, A1), ICRS at epoch J2016.0, from the archived row src/objects/alcyone/source/photometry/gaia-dr3-source.csv; cross-identification HD 23630, HR 1165, HIP 17702: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=Gaia+DR3+66714384142368256
sources.distance: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17702: distance 123.609 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.052), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 123.609 +/- 6.428 pc; Gaia DR3 gives this source no parallax (a two-parameter solution)
sources.properMotion: Gaia DR3 source 66714384142368256 is a two-parameter solution with no proper motion; zero is assumed (at 124 pc, 1 mas/yr would be 1 km/s across the sky)
sources.radialVelocity: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 66714384142368256 (quality B), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2006AstL...32..759G/abstract)
